m.d: An effect is something that is caused by something else.
m.e: His comments had a visible effect on those who heard it.

m.d: If a law, agreement, change, etc. takes effect, it officially begins.
m.e: The closing of the company takes effect at midnight.

m.d: A sound effect is a way to make a sound for a performance artificially.
m.e: The used a lot of normal materials to create the sound effects for the show.

m.d: If you effect a change, you make it happen.
m.e: I will effect the change without your help.

m.d: The amount of work that is done on something.
m.e: A great amount of effort was put into this event; we had over 4,000 visitors.

m.d: An effective strategy, treatment, method, etc is one that works well as planned.
m.e: Teachers are using instructional strategies that are most effective in helping students learn.

m.d: If you have effective command, consent, control, etc., you have it in practice but not officially.
m.e: The students had effective control over what the teacher would include on the test.

m.d: If a law, agreement, change, etc. becomes effective, it officially begins.
m.e: The new rules about ball size are effective next season.

m.d: You use effective to tell when something starts officially.
m.e: Effective next week, all employees will wear the new uniform.

m.d: If something is efficient, it can do a lot but uses very little time, energy, money, etc.
m.e: He wastes a lot of time talking, and isn't very efficient at work.

m.d: If something is done effectively, it is done in a way that is effective.
Efficiency is the state or quality of being efficient.
Efficiencies are steps that can be taken to make things more efficient.
If something is done efficiently, it is done in an efficient manner.
